findings.title: Denial cache blocks the DB requery this PR adds
findings.body: Check consults permDenialCache before cached permissions or the database, and on any final deny it stores that key for shortCacheTTL (30s). A later grant never clears the entry, so the new "requery when the scope is missing from cached permissions" path is skipped and Check keeps returning Allowed=false. That is the creator flow this PR is meant to fix: a check before the dashboard/folder permission row exists (or before a just-created parent is in the folder tree) records a deny, and the follow-up open still fails until the denial entry expires even if getIdentityPermissions would now allow it. Revocation stays cached on the allow path, so denials are strictly stickier than grants.

findings.title: Denial cache key collides when UIDs contain underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name, and parent with "_" and no delimiter that cannot appear in a UID. Grafana short UIDs may contain underscores, so name "foo" + parent "bar_baz" and name "foo_bar" + parent "baz" produce the same key. A cached deny for one resource then makes Check return Allowed=false for a different resource the user is allowed to access, for the full denial TTL.

findings.title: List still serves stale permission cache
findings.body: List returns getCachedIdentityPermissions immediately on a cache hit and never requeries when a newly created dashboard or folder scope is absent. Check was changed to fall through to the DB in that case, so after creation Check can allow a resource that List still omits for up to shortCacheTTL (30s). Callers that "fetch" newly created dashboards/folders via List keep the bug this PR describes.
